body_md:
#### Rolling Dice
Kriegsmesser uses six sided Dice for practically everything. Some of these are special, in the sense that they have unique behaviors when rolled. However, these behaviors are procedural, not actual properties of the Dice. Hence, any six sided Die will do. The special varieties of Dice are:
- **Chaos Dice**: which are six sided Dice that have unique contextual effects when rolling a six. Rolling a 6 is almost always bad.
- **Pools**: which are arbitrarily sized collections of Dice, rolled together. Pools have effects depending on how many Dice roll a certain face. For example, Pools of Chaos Dice usually have effects depending on how many roll a 6.
#### Skill Tests
These are used to adjudicate a task or course of action that you declare in-character that have a plausible chance of success or failure. Some mechanically codified tasks, like Actions, might call for a Test of some kind in their description, or the GM can require one of you. To make a Skill Test, roll 2d6 and add both your Tier and Ability Bonus.
*Unskilled Tests*
	You can still make a Test without a given Skill, but you can only add your Ability Bonus.

**Evaluation**
compare the result to a Difficulty or 'DC', a number given by the GM. If your roll is equal to or higher than the DC, you succeed.

**Adjusting the Difficulty of a Test**
Difficulty has a default value of 8, but is adjusted very frequently. When a Test is adjusted, the Difficulty will increase or decrease by an amount implied by the circumstance.

A good guide to the "feel" of Difficulty as well as a rough statistical estimate can be derived from your Tier as follows:
**Minor**/*80%*: T+6| **Moderate**/*60%*: T+8| **Major**/*30%*: T+10| **Extreme**/*10%*: T+12|
- *If you lack the Skill, default T to 0 for this chart.*
- *Adding a Boon or Bane moves these odds by about 10% with diminishing returns for each additional Die.*

**Resistance**
When you make a Test against a Creature, they Resist, raising the DC by its Tier. So, making an Attack against a Creature of Tier 1 has a DC of 9 (8+1). Likewise, when making Tests against a Creature, and the Test is against a Skill, the Difficulty is raised by their Tier again, twice the increase.
*Tests Against Skilled Targets*
	- Tier 1| *DC*: 10
	- Tier 2| *DC*: 12
	- Tier 3| *DC*: 14
*Tests Against Unskilled Targets*
	- Tier 1| *DC*: 9
	- Tier 2| *DC*: 10
	- Tier 3| *DC*: 11
*Unaware Targets*
	In the exception of the above, Creatures that cannot Detect you (against whom you have Full Cover) and fail to Target (in the case of Partial Cover) you cannot Resist. Against such a Target, all Tests have the default DC of 8. ([[d_Senses, Targeting, Cover, Spaces, and Environmental Hazards]])

**Critical Success and Failure**
When you make a Skill Test, there is a remote possibility that your result is critical.
*Critical Success*
	- `If you roll a natural 12 and pass the Test DC.`
	Critical successes are the "best case" outcome of a Test. Most Actions will have explicit consequences for a Critical Success, but if there no pre-written benefit, the GM should confer some additional benefit.
*Critical Failure*
	- `Following any roll of a natural 2, even if you would have otherwise succeeded.`
	Critically failing a Test is the inverse, you fail and drastically so. Critical failures provoke Moderate Panic Risk in addition to the negative outcome of the Test.

**Boons and Banes**
These are d6 that can be rolled along with any other d6, which curve the rolled result a bit in either direction, up for Boons, down for Banes. Rolling 2d6 with a Boon means you would roll 3d6 and take the highest two, or the lowest 2 for a Bane.

Banes and Boons subtract from one another, so a roll with both a Bane and a Boon is a roll with neither.

**Ability Bonuses**
At certain thresholds of Ability, you gain an Ability Bonus to Tests made with corresponding Skills. In general, you obtain an Ability Bonus to a Skill equal to 1/6th (or one for every six) of the Ability, rounded down (meaning that at 5 or less, the Bonus would be 0.)
*Ability Bonus Thresholds*
	6: `+1`| 12: `+2`| 18: `+3`|...
- *Body Skills*: Vitality, Traversal, Unity.
- *Mind Skills*: Immanence, Resolve, Creation, Luminance.
- *Reflex Skills*: Action,  Potence, Darkness.
*Ability Bonuses and Specialized Tests*
	In general, Ability Bonuses can be applied to a Specialized Test, provided the Skill and Discipline correspond match the Ability.
*Dynamic Bonuses*
	Strain can reduce your Abilities, and when they fall below one of the Thresholds, you lose the corresponding Bonus. For example, if your Mind was 12, your Ability Bonus would normally be +2. Yet, if you suffered Strain, it would reduce by 1 (because your Mind would fall below 12). If your Mind fell below 6, you would lose the Bonus entirely until you shed enough Strain.

**Skill Etiquette**
In general, it is a faux pas to simply declare a Skill Test, or to argue with the GM about which Skills are requested of you for Tests. Of course, you are the one who decides the Actions, Feats, and activities of your PC. Nonetheless, engaging in so-called "mother-may-I" behavior, wherein you negotiate with the GM at length, is usually a bad idea. This slows the game for other players and, unless handled with tact and maturity, can depreciate the experience for most others. Further, it doesn't even make sense to do this, as AMPs, DIMs, and Difficulty require input from the GM, but radically change the outcome of a roll.

There is no rule, per-se, against doing this, and your judgement can help everyone learn, including your GM. Simply keep this as a rule of thumb: Skills are asked for by the GM when you take an Action, Feat, or do something in Character. Declaring "I roll Luminance!" is the wrong approach to finding traps.
#### Coin-Flip
Sometimes, a Skill Test is too small-scale or too predictable for truly random chance. In such cases, employ a Coin-Flip. The GM will briefly describe the two possible outcomes and ask Players to pick their preferred face, "calling" the Flip. The GM will then flip the coin and adjudicate results accordingly.AMPs and DIMs, should they apply to a Coin-Flip, are extra flips of the coin. A Flip with a DIM takes the worse result, while a Flip with aAMP does the opposite.
### Skills in Specific
With all of the above in mind, we can discuss the 10 Skills.
- **Amount**: Each Character has 5 Skills, and each is scaled by their Tier.
- **Principals and Limits**: The Skills of Action, Potency, Vitality, and Resolve are your Principal Skills. These are used to make Attacks and constitute your defenses against the Actions of others. *You cannot have more than 2 Principal Skills.*
- **Implications**: Skills can also have a psychological dimension, in addition to the practical. A Character with Darkness and Action would be quite a bit different from one with Immanence, Potency, and Vitality. This can give you a clue on how to roleplay them, should you need some guidance.
**Immanence**
This Skill represents the continual pursuit of higher things. You can use Immanence to intuit abstractions, comprehend complex problems, and construct logical connections.
**Action**
This Skill represents the practiced, instant exercise of force. You can use Action to impose your strength, perform athletic feats, make snap judgements, and resolve problems under pressure.
- *Action is a Principal Skill used to make and defend against Melee Attacks.*
**Potence**
This Skill represents trained coordination through time. You can use Potence to balance yourself, to make and execute plans, construct inferences, hypothesize, and intuit danger.
- *Potence is a Principal Skill used to make and defend against Ranged Attacks.*
**Vitality**
This Skill represents cultivated physical robustness and health. You can use Vitality to act out raw strength and speed, assess and aid those who suffer harm, express the force of your passion, and endure physical trials.
- *Vitality is a Principal Skill used to make and defend against Melee Attacks.*
**Resolve**
This Skill represents honed intention and force of will. You can use Resolve to concentrate through immense physical tasks, impress with your presence and strong affect, force intellectual problems through sheer deliberation, and pry answers from even the most resistant situations and persons.
- *Resolve is a Principal Skill used to make and defend against Ranged Attacks.*
**Creation**
This Skill represents the channeled ability to create. You can use Creation to design complex devices, construct from raw materials, make art and artifice, employ alchemy, assess the creations of others and design armaments. Creation is also the basis of repairing and restoring things. You can use it to fix Ruined gear and perform Surgery.
**Traversal**
This Skill represents the trained faculty for navigation. You can use Traversal to negotiate precarious terrain, force your way through obstacles, decipher networks of relationship and trade, assess localities, and circumvent confusion.
**Darkness**
This Skill represents the methodologies which distort and conceal. You can use Darkness to lay snares and play tricks, deceive, forge documents, break locks, assess marks, and provoke fear.
**Luminance**
This Skill represents the hunt for the truth. You can use Luminance to physically examine, sift out a liar, find holes in forgeries and illusions, sense dangers and hidden things, and wring the truth from a stone.
**Unity**
This Skill represents the cultivation of leadership and authority. You can use Unity to give a rallying shout, spur a charge, manage an organization, detect unrest, and decry chaos.

#### Rolling Dice
Kriegsmesser uses six sided Dice for practically everything. Some of these are special, in the sense that they have unique behaviors when rolled. However, these behaviors are procedural, not actual properties of the Dice. Hence, any six sided Die will do. The special varieties of Dice are:
- **Chaos Dice**: which are six sided Dice that have unique contextual effects when rolling a six. Rolling a 6 is almost always bad.
- **Pools**: which are arbitrarily sized collections of Dice, rolled together. Pools have effects depending on how many Dice roll a certain face. For example, Pools of Chaos Dice usually have effects depending on how many roll a 6.
#### Skill Tests
These are used to adjudicate a task or course of action that you declare in-character that have a plausible chance of success or failure. Some mechanically codified tasks, like Actions, might call for a Test of some kind in their description, or the GM can require one of you. To make a Skill Test, roll 2d6 and add both your Tier and Ability Bonus.
*Unskilled Tests*
	You can still make a Test without a given Skill, but you can only add your Ability Bonus.

**Evaluation**
compare the result to a Difficulty or 'DC', a number given by the GM. If your roll is equal to or higher than the DC, you succeed.

**Adjusting the Difficulty of a Test**
Difficulty has a default value of 8, but is adjusted very frequently. When a Test is adjusted, the Difficulty will increase or decrease by an amount implied by the circumstance.

A good guide to the "feel" of Difficulty as well as a rough statistical estimate can be derived from your Tier as follows:
**Minor**/*80%*: T+6| **Moderate**/*60%*: T+8| **Major**/*30%*: T+10| **Extreme**/*10%*: T+12|
- *If you lack the Skill, default T to 0 for this chart.*
- *Adding a Boon or Bane moves these odds by about 10% with diminishing returns for each additional Die.*

**Resistance**
When you make a Test against a Creature, they Resist, raising the DC by its Tier. So, making an Attack against a Creature of Tier 1 has a DC of 9 (8+1). Likewise, when making Tests against a Creature, and the Test is against a Skill, the Difficulty is raised by their Tier again, twice the increase.
*Tests Against Skilled Targets*
	- Tier 1| *DC*: 10
	- Tier 2| *DC*: 12
	- Tier 3| *DC*: 14
*Tests Against Unskilled Targets*
	- Tier 1| *DC*: 9
	- Tier 2| *DC*: 10
	- Tier 3| *DC*: 11
*Unaware Targets*
	In the exception of the above, Creatures that cannot Detect you (against whom you have Full Cover) and fail to Target (in the case of Partial Cover) you cannot Resist. Against such a Target, all Tests have the default DC of 8. ([[d_Senses, Targeting, Cover, Spaces, and Environmental Hazards]])

**Critical Success and Failure**
When you make a Skill Test, there is a remote possibility that your result is critical.
*Critical Success*
	- `If you roll a natural 12 and pass the Test DC.`
	Critical successes are the "best case" outcome of a Test. Most Actions will have explicit consequences for a Critical Success, but if there no pre-written benefit, the GM should confer some additional benefit.
*Critical Failure*
	- `Following any roll of a natural 2, even if you would have otherwise succeeded.`
	Critically failing a Test is the inverse, you fail and drastically so. Critical failures provoke Moderate Panic Risk in addition to the negative outcome of the Test.

**Boons and Banes**
These are d6 that can be rolled along with any other d6, which curve the rolled result a bit in either direction, up for Boons, down for Banes. Rolling 2d6 with a Boon means you would roll 3d6 and take the highest two, or the lowest 2 for a Bane.

Banes and Boons subtract from one another, so a roll with both a Bane and a Boon is a roll with neither.

**Ability Bonuses**
At certain thresholds of Ability, you gain an Ability Bonus to Tests made with corresponding Skills. In general, you obtain an Ability Bonus to a Skill equal to 1/6th (or one for every six) of the Ability, rounded down (meaning that at 5 or less, the Bonus would be 0.)
*Ability Bonus Thresholds*
	6: `+1`| 12: `+2`| 18: `+3`|...
- *Body Skills*: Vitality, Traversal, Unity.
- *Mind Skills*: Immanence, Resolve, Creation, Luminance.
- *Reflex Skills*: Action,  Potence, Darkness.
*Ability Bonuses and Specialized Tests*
	In general, Ability Bonuses can be applied to a Specialized Test, provided the Skill and Discipline correspond match the Ability.
*Dynamic Bonuses*
	Strain can reduce your Abilities, and when they fall below one of the Thresholds, you lose the corresponding Bonus. For example, if your Mind was 12, your Ability Bonus would normally be +2. Yet, if you suffered Strain, it would reduce by 1 (because your Mind would fall below 12). If your Mind fell below 6, you would lose the Bonus entirely until you shed enough Strain.

**Skill Etiquette**
In general, it is a faux pas to simply declare a Skill Test, or to argue with the GM about which Skills are requested of you for Tests. Of course, you are the one who decides the Actions, Feats, and activities of your PC. Nonetheless, engaging in so-called "mother-may-I" behavior, wherein you negotiate with the GM at length, is usually a bad idea. This slows the game for other players and, unless handled with tact and maturity, can depreciate the experience for most others. Further, it doesn't even make sense to do this, as AMPs, DIMs, and Difficulty require input from the GM, but radically change the outcome of a roll.

There is no rule, per-se, against doing this, and your judgement can help everyone learn, including your GM. Simply keep this as a rule of thumb: Skills are asked for by the GM when you take an Action, Feat, or do something in Character. Declaring "I roll Luminance!" is the wrong approach to finding traps.
#### Coin-Flip
Sometimes, a Skill Test is too small-scale or too predictable for truly random chance. In such cases, employ a Coin-Flip. The GM will briefly describe the two possible outcomes and ask Players to pick their preferred face, "calling" the Flip. The GM will then flip the coin and adjudicate results accordingly.AMPs and DIMs, should they apply to a Coin-Flip, are extra flips of the coin. A Flip with a DIM takes the worse result, while a Flip with aAMP does the opposite.
### Skills in Specific
With all of the above in mind, we can discuss the 10 Skills.
- **Amount**: Each Character has 5 Skills, and each is scaled by their Tier.
- **Principals and Limits**: The Skills of Action, Potency, Vitality, and Resolve are your Principal Skills. These are used to make Attacks and constitute your defenses against the Actions of others. *You cannot have more than 2 Principal Skills.*
- **Implications**: Skills can also have a psychological dimension, in addition to the practical. A Character with Darkness and Action would be quite a bit different from one with Immanence, Potency, and Vitality. This can give you a clue on how to roleplay them, should you need some guidance.
**Immanence**
This Skill represents the continual pursuit of higher things. You can use Immanence to intuit abstractions, comprehend complex problems, and construct logical connections.
**Action**
This Skill represents the practiced, instant exercise of force. You can use Action to impose your strength, perform athletic feats, make snap judgements, and resolve problems under pressure.
- *Action is a Principal Skill used to make and defend against Melee Attacks.*
**Potence**
This Skill represents trained coordination through time. You can use Potence to balance yourself, to make and execute plans, construct inferences, hypothesize, and intuit danger.
- *Potence is a Principal Skill used to make and defend against Ranged Attacks.*
**Vitality**
This Skill represents cultivated physical robustness and health. You can use Vitality to act out raw strength and speed, assess and aid those who suffer harm, express the force of your passion, and endure physical trials.
- *Vitality is a Principal Skill used to make and defend against Melee Attacks.*
**Resolve**
This Skill represents honed intention and force of will. You can use Resolve to concentrate through immense physical tasks, impress with your presence and strong affect, force intellectual problems through sheer deliberation, and pry answers from even the most resistant situations and persons.
- *Resolve is a Principal Skill used to make and defend against Ranged Attacks.*
**Creation**
This Skill represents the channeled ability to create. You can use Creation to design complex devices, construct from raw materials, make art and artifice, employ alchemy, assess the creations of others and design armaments. Creation is also the basis of repairing and restoring things. You can use it to fix Ruined gear and perform Surgery.
**Traversal**
This Skill represents the trained faculty for navigation. You can use Traversal to negotiate precarious terrain, force your way through obstacles, decipher networks of relationship and trade, assess localities, and circumvent confusion.
**Darkness**
This Skill represents the methodologies which distort and conceal. You can use Darkness to lay snares and play tricks, deceive, forge documents, break locks, assess marks, and provoke fear.
**Luminance**
This Skill represents the hunt for the truth. You can use Luminance to physically examine, sift out a liar, find holes in forgeries and illusions, sense dangers and hidden things, and wring the truth from a stone.
**Unity**
This Skill represents the cultivation of leadership and authority. You can use Unity to give a rallying shout, spur a charge, manage an organization, detect unrest, and decry chaos.

name: Ability Thresholds and Bonuses
summary: The three dimensions of a Character in terms of Ability measure their basic capacities, their fundamental strengths without Skill.
body_md:
## The Three Abilities
The three dimensions of a Character in terms of Ability measure their basic capacities, their fundamental strengths without Skill.

**Thresholds of Ability**
Once your Abilities reach a multiple of six, 6, 12, and 18, you obtain certain benefits. Firstly, an Ability Bonus to Skills related to that Ability and, second, a Threshold Feat corresponding to the value of your Base Ability.
*Thresholds are Permanent and Intrinsic*
	When you gain a Threshold Feat, you don't lose it, though the effects of Strain may reduce its magnitude. Conversely, you only gain a Threshold Feat when your Base Ability reaches that value. Hence, only Ability Advancements from EXP or other, extraneous effects that specifically hit your Base can grant a Threshold Feat.
*Conditional Function*
	Whenever a Threshold Feat refers to your Ability Bonus, it refers to your current Bonus, which can diminish as you suffer ever more Strain. While you never lose these Feats, their benefits might be negated by this change. For example, if a Feat added your Ability Bonus to a Test while under enough Strain to reduce your Bonus to 0, the Feat would also add 0.
#### Body
Strength, power, stability. Body reflects your physical development in terms of active capacity to effect the world and resist Damage.

**Body Thresholds**
	6: `+1`| 12: `+2`| 18: `+3`|...
- *Body Skills*: Vitality, Traversal, Unity.

Threshold 6: **Power Attack**| Ability Bonus: `Begins at +1`
	Your strength allows you to amplify the destructive power of your Strikes.
	`When you make a Melee Attack to Strike with a Weapon (including Improvized but not Unarmed), you can suffer a penalty up to your Body Bonus to make the Damage more Vicious by an equal amount.`

Threshold 12: **Greater Resistance**| Ability Bonus: `Increases to +2`
	While unable to prevent harm, the refinement of Body can resist it.
	`You may add your Body Bonus to your Injury Risk. If this rolls outside the range of the Table (13 or more) you avoid all effects.`

Threshold 18: **Indomitable**| Ability Bonus: `Increases to +3`
	At the apex of physical achievement, only the greatest of peril can wear you down.
	`You gain Resistence to all Physical Damage, up to your Body Bonus.`
### Mind
Apprehension, intuition, will. Mind reflects the force of your mental acuity. Not necessarily a matter of traditional "smarts", Mind is the power to overcome problems and see connections in the world around you.

**Mind Thresholds**
	6: `+1`| 12: `+2`| 18: `+3`|...
- *Mind Skills*: Immanence, Resolve, Creation, Luminance.

Threshold 6: **Wits**| Ability Bonus: `Begins at +1`
	Knowing yourself, you might heighten the magnitude of your victories.
	`The range of natural roll you need to Critically Succeed is increased by your Ability Bonus; this allows you to Critically Succeed on a natural 11, 10, and so on as your Bonus grows.`

Threshold 12: **Cunning**| Ability Bonus: `Increases to +2`
	Knowing the world, even certain failures can be reversed.
	`When you fail a Skill Test but not by more than your Ability Bonus, you can suffer 1 Strain and succeed instead. This can also be applied to Preemption rolls, as if they were Skill Tests.`

Threshold 18: **Prediction**| Ability Bonus: `Increases to +3`
	Knowing the Other, each exchange is riddle; its solution gives way to your uncontested superiority.
	`When you Preempt a Creature, you can Critically Succeed if your roll exceeds their Initiative and the natural roll is a 12(adjusted by your Wits). Critical Successes confer the following benefits:`
	- `If you Preempted the Target just after they declare an Action, you gain AP equal to the amount they intended to spend.`
	- `The Target becomes more Vulnerable to you, equal to your Ability Bonus.`

#### Reflex
Speed, dynamism, reactivity. Reflex reflects your inner potential for motion, both to propel yourself and in swift response to sudden stimulus.

**Reflex Thresholds**
	6: `+1`| 12: `+2`| 18: `+3`|...
- *Reflex Skills*: Action, Potence, Darkness.

Threshold 6: **Unnatural Agility**| Ability Bonus: `Begins at +1`
	You are almost never off your guard, replete with Reflex, each step lighter than the last.
	`Each Turn, you gain Agility up to your Ability Bonus. Agility can be spent like AP, but only for Reactions. You also gain half as much when rolling Initiative, rounded down.`

Threshold 12: **Dodge**| Ability Bonus: `Increases to +2`
	The wind shifts, and you as well.
	`When you are the Target of an Attack, you can spend AP as a Reaction, up to your Ability Bonus, to inflict that many Banes on the Test.`

Threshold 18: **The Apex of Motion**| Ability Bonus: `Increases to +3`
	Few, if any, match your pace anymore.
	`You can spend two Agility to gain one AP at any time.`

name: Health
summary: Kriegsmesser measures your durability and current state in a few ways. Managing these is key to surviving an Expedition.
body_md:
Kriegsmesser measures your durability and current state in a few ways. Managing these is key to surviving an Expedition.

**Your Reserve**
Like a literal Durability, your Reserve is your resistance to fatigue. It has a value, equal to:
	*Reserve*=(Your Tier)+(Your Body Bonus)
- This is measured in a line on the upper border of your Sheet.

**Strain**
This is a universal measure of duress, and comes in three types:
	- *Standard*: expires in ten Minutes.
	- *Persistent*: shed by Resting.
	- *Permanent*: Inury-related, and requires healing.
- This is measured with your Reserve, for clarity of purpose and function.
*What Strain Does*
	When you suffer Strain in excess of your Reserve, all your Abilities and derived statistics fall by the same amount. When any of these falls to zero, you are Incapacitated.
#### The Core Gameplay Loops

**Tracking Strain**
When you suffer Strain, you mark it below your Reserve, checking a box with the corresponding symbol:
- *Standard Strain*: { / }
- *Persistent Strain*: { X }
- *Permanent Strain*: { * }
*Priority*
	More severe Strain is moved to the left of the tracker, facilitated by the marks made. So:
	- If you had three Standard Strain, that would be three slashes on the track.
	- If you suffered one Persistent, you would mark the left-most space with an X, and move the slash to the fourth space.

**Taxing an Ability**
Another way in which your Abilities can be diminished, you may Tax an Ability before making a relevant Skill Test to automatically Succeed (unless Success is impossible for some reason.)
*Cost*
	Taxing an Ability reduces it by one until you Catch your Breath. ([[d_Rest and Catching your Breath]].)
*Relevance*
	Which Ability you may Tax for which Test depends on its relationship to that Skill. ([[1_Making Characters/f-Ability Thresholds and Bonuses|f-Ability Thresholds and Bonuses]])
*Recourse*
	If you are denied the Success for Taxing an Ability for any reason, you do not reduce the Ability.

**Incapacitation**
When Incapacitated, you black-out, and are Unconscious for 1d6 Minutes. While Unconscious, you are Helpless, making all successful Attacks instantly Lethal. At the end of this time, you shed all Standard Strain and all Persistent Strain over your Reserve.
*Overload*
	If you have enough Permanent Strain from Injuries to Incapacitate you, you are Unconscious until this is no longer the case.

**Bleeding**
When you suffer the Bleeding Condition, you begin to rapidly lose blood. After a number of Rounds equal to your Natural Body value (absent the influence of your Strain or Taxation), you are Incapacitated. After twice that amount of time, you die. *Bleeding can be stopped by First-Aid.*

**Damage and Injuries**
When you are Attacked with a Weapon, fall from some height, or are Damaged by any means, you Risk being Injured.
*Damage Types*
	Instances of Damage comes in Types, corresponding to its source. Falling inflicts Crushing Damage, an arrow inflicts Piercing Damage, etc.
	- The Damage Type determines what Injury Risk Table you should roll from.
	- If an Attack inflicts multiple types of Damage, the Attacker chooses one as the primary effect.
*Threat*
	The amount of Damage dealt in any instance depends on the Type, for example, Cutting has a Base Damage of 1.
	- Objects and Armor are Notched up to this value when Damaged.
	- Damage is modified by the Vicious Trait, increasing (or reducing) it by a number of steps.
	- *If an instance of Damage would be less than one, it is Blunted instead. Blunted Damage inflicts a single Notch against Objects, Items, and Armor, and Creatures automatically roll a natural 12 on their Injury Risk for Blunted Damage.
*Injury Risk*
	When you suffer Damage, you roll from an Injury Table corresponding to the triggering Damage Type. ([[b_Attacks, Damage, and Injuries]])
	- When Injured, you suffer Permanent Strain equal the Damage.
	- An Injury has a Severity, which determines how it can be removed.
	- The Permanent Strain from an Injury is only shed when the Injury is removed.

**Armor**
This is a kind of Equipment with the ability to mitigate Damage. Armor has a Durability and a list of Damage Ratings.
*Avoiding Damage*
	When you would be Damaged by something your Armor is Rated for, you are unharmed. However, the Armor suffers Notches equal to the Damage.
*Breaking*
	Like any other Item, your Armor Breaks when Notched beyond its Durability. When your armor Breaks, you suffer the remaining Damage instead. For example, if your Armor had a Durability of 3, two Notches already, and suffered 4 Crushing Damage, the armor would be Notched twice, Break, and you would suffer the remaining 2 Crushing Damage.

name: Attacks, Damage, and Injuries
summary: These are Skill Tests made with Weapons to harm a Target, usually by inflicting Damage. Attacks use one of four Principle Skills, and are Resisted by the Same Skill used to make them.
body_md:
#### Attacks
These are Skill Tests made with Weapons to harm a Target, usually by inflicting Damage. Attacks use one of four Principle Skills, and are Resisted by the Same Skill used to make them.

**Damage**
Damage from an Attack depends on its Traits (or those of the Weapon used to make it). The Base Damage is set by a Type, Cutting Damage has a Base of 1 for example. Further, the Vicious Trait increases this amount. So, an Attack with a Vicious_2 Cutting Weapon deals 3 Damage.

**Melee Attacks**
Made against close Targets, Melee Weapons are either made with Weapons or Unarmed, using the skills of Vitality or Action.

**Ranged Attacks**
Made at a distance, Ranged Attacks always involve a Weapon, and use the Skills of Potence or Resolve.

**Gaming Attacks**
Characters can only have two of four Principle Skills, and Attacks are made with non-overlapping sets. In Character Creation, it's important note this and plan accordingly.

- **Bulk**: The amount it weighs, measured in Bulk. This is especially important for Melee Weapons.
- **Misc Traits**: How many Hands one needs to Wield it, what Type of Damage it inflicts, and other properties go here.

**Melee Weapons**
Used against close foes, Melee Weapons require an amount of strength to use effectively.

**Ranged Weapons**
Able to pick out distant Targets, Ranged Weapons offer the advantages of both relative safety and scope, but are often harder than Melee Attacks.
- *The Trait of Range*: If a Target is further away than the Weapon's Range, then the Attack is made with a Bane and is Harder by 1 for every two Meters.

**Unarmed and Improvised Attacks**
When you Attack without a Weapon, or with something no traditionally classified as one, use the following profiles:
*Unarmed Weaponry*
	*Tier*: (Your Own)| *Damage*: `Crushing`|
	*Accuracy*: -T| *Bulk*: 0
	*Traits*: `Blunt`
*Improvised Weaponry*
	*Tier*: (Your Own)| *Damage*: `Varies`
	*Accuracy*: -T| *Bulk*: `Varies`
	*Traits*: `Clumsy`
	- `The Damage of these Weapons is decided by the GM. Sharp Objects usually inflict Cutting or Piercing, but most inflict Crushing. If the Object's Bulk is greater than the Target's this becomes Traumatic Damage.`
	- `You must be able to vertically lift something to use it this way.`

**Simple Attack Reference**
The following steps outline what the usual procedure is when making an Attack:
- *1*: Make an Attack against a Target.
- *2_a*: If the Target is wearing Armor, it is Notched equal to the Damage.
- *2_b*: Otherwise, the Target rolls from an Injury Table, corresponding to the Damage Type, and suffers Permanent Strain (equal to the Damage) from any Injuries.

**Weakness and Resistance**
Sometimes, a Creature can be Weak or especially Resistant to a kind of Damage.
- *Weakness_*: When a Creature has the Weakness Trait to x Damage Type or Types, that Damage is more Vicious against them by x.
- *Resistance_x*: When a Creature has the Resistance Trait to x Type or Types of Damage, that Damage is less Vicious against them. As usual, Damage is Blunted when reduced below 1. *Blunted Damage gives the Target an automatic 12 on their Risk, and only inflicts a single Notch.*
*Scale*
	Viciousness increases (or decreases) the amount of an instance of Damage. So both of these Traits usually have a value attached (if no value is listed, assume 1). So, against a Creature with Weakeness-3_Crushing, any Crushing Damage would be more Vicious by 3, raising it to 4, from its Base Damage of 1, all else equal.
*Equipment*
	Weakness and Resistance applies both ways to and from Equipment. So, the Creature in the above scenario would suffer four Notches to any Armor it was wearing from Crushing Damage. Likewise, equipped with something that granted Resistance-3_Crushing, the Creature's innate Weakness would be canceled out.
*Multiplicity*
	If some instance of Damage has more than one Type, the Attacker chooses which is applied.
	- Weaknesses and Resistances may only apply to the single Damage Type.
	- Only one Damage Type can be chosen for this purpose.

#### Injury Risk
When Damaged by something, you roll from the corresponding Table, suffering whatever the result stipulates.
- Several types of Damage have general rules, like Cuts being harder to Bandage, Crushing Injuries Stun you, etc.
- Injuries inflict Permanent Strain equal to the Damage, in addition to anything caused by the result.

**Injury Severity**
- *-*: `Instead of an Injury or Permanent Strain, you only suffer some effect or Condition for a given Duration.`
- *Minor*: `These Injuries are removed by First-Aid`
- *Moderate*: `These Injuries are removed by Recovery.`
- *Major*: `These Injuries are removed by Surgical Treatment.`
- *Lethal*: `You cannot remove a Lethal Injury, as you are simply dead.`

Damage Types have a Base Damage value (for Strain and Notching Items) as well as an array of Injuries they can inflict. Likewise, Damage Types can have Traits:
- **Physical Damage**: cuts, impact, explosons, stabs, etc.
- **Energy Damage**: burns from less definite forms of power.
- **Arcane/Magical Damage**: inflicted by Spells and Rituals.

Physical Damage: **Cutting**
	*Base Damage*: 1
Incisions and wounds of separation. Cuts are gruesome work, an even uglier way to die. `Injuries from Cutting are harder to Treat or provide First-Aid, inflicting a Bane on associated Tests.`
- *8-12*: Minor| *Superficial Cut*: A line of cold crimson, a weeping incision below the surface. `You begin to Bleed.`
- *4-7*: Moderate| *Gash*: Grimacing, open across and in-through sinew. `You begin to Bleed and Risk Minor Panic.`
- *2-3*: Major|  *Arterial Vent*: Blood pours from the opening, its vacuum welcoming ice into your core. `You begin to Bleed and Risk Major Panic.`

Physical Damage: **Crushing**
	*Base Damage*: 1
The impressions of fists and hammers. These Injuries are not usually lethal, but generally debilitating. `Crushing Injuries do not inflict Bleeding. When you suffer one, you become Stunned for 1d6 Turns.`
- *11-12*: -| *Wheezer*: A blow that steals the breath, but little more. `You are Stunned for one Round and suffer 1 Strain.`
- *7-10*: Minor| *Dazed*: You come to your senses, if just. `You suffer 1d6 Strain and are Off-Balance.`
- *6*: Minor| *Tenderized*: A blow that leaves more than a mark, a shatter-point that you must guard. `You suffer 1 Strain and are one more Vulnerable.`
- *4-5*: Minor| *Dislocation*: Something comes loose. `You Risk Moderate Panic, and lose the use of 1 Limb, chosen by the Attacker. If this is a leg, your Movement is halved. Flying Creatures fall if this is a wing.`
- *2-3*: Major| *Thoracic Fracture*: A crack in your chest, each strenuous move comes with a grinding agony. `You suffer Major Panic from pain, which inflicts Persistant Strain. Each time you are Injured after this, you Risk additional Moderate Panic.`

Physical Damage: **Piercing**
	*Base Damage*: 2
Harm from stabs and arrows. While superior in piercing defenses, this tends to be a very unpredictable form of Risk. `When you suffer a Injury of Minor or greater Severity, you begin to Bleed.`
- *8-12*: -| *Graze*: Your skin stings and ears whine from a brush much closer than comfortable. `You are Off-Balance for 1 Round and suffer one Strain.`
- *6-7*: Minor| *Remote Puncture*: A hot line drawn through a foot or hand. `One of your extremities at random is Injured. Tests with Injured hands are penalized by 1, and each foot or mobility-limb penalizes Movement by 1.`
- *4-5*: Moderate| *Gutshot*: Your breath catches with the sudden loss of pressure within your abdominal cavity. `You Risk Minor Panic, and this Injury is automatically Infected.`
- *2-3*: Major| *Rent Lung*: A wheeze escapes your mouth, a dry-wet rasp betraying internal compromise. `You Risk Moderate Panic from Pain and suffer a Penalty of 2 to your Body.`

Physical Damage: **Impaling**
	*Base Damage*: 3
The greater form of Piercing Damage, Impaling Damage is much the same, but far more lethal.
- *7-12*: -| *Graze*: Your ears ring, following a trench cut in the air. `You suffer one Strain, and are Off-Balance and Stunned for 1 Round.`
- *3-6*: Major| *Socket Piercer*: Grinding friction from a joint rendered useless. `You lose the use of one of your limbs entirely (chosen by the Attacker). If this is a leg, your Movement is cut in half, suffering this to both legs makes your Prone. Flying Creatures begin to fall from this Injury.`
- *2*: Lethal| *Headshot*: Iron through the skull, taking thought and life along the line of flight. `You die.`

Physical Damage: **Rending**
	*Base Damage*: 3
The greater form of Cutting Damage, hewing chops and sweeps of lethal potential. `Harder to treat, as Cutting Injuries. All results, even a Swipe, cause Bleeding.`
- *11-12*: -| *Swipe*: A near-blow, the closeness its own kind of harm. `You Risk Minor Panic and are Off-Balance for 1 Round.`
- *8-10*: Moderate| *Laceration*: `You instantly lose half your remaining time to Bleed-Out.`
- *3-7*: Major| *Loss*: Nothing left but a bleeding stump. `You instantly lose half your remaining time to Bleed-Out and you lose a non-critical limb or bodypart of the Attacker's choice, with all the consequences following to Actions and Senses. Recovery does not restore the Lost part.`
- *2*: Lethal| *Decapitation*: `You die.`

Physical Damage: **Traumatic**
	*Base Damage*: 3
The greater form of Crushing Damage, tremendous force, limbs of awful size, falling beams, crushing and crashing structures. `Unlike Crushing Damage, all results of Minor or greater Severity cause Bleeding.`
- *7-12*: -| *Traumatic Graze*: You roll away, confused but unharmed. `You suffer one Strain and are Off-Balance for 1 Full_Turn.`
- *3-6*: Major| *Break*: Recoiling, you live, but terribly wounded. `You suffer the combined effects of a rolled Crushing and Cutting Injury.`
- *2*: Lethal| *Collapse*: The force was simply too great. `You die.`

Physical Damage: **Explosive**
	*Base Damage*: 4
Shattering reports and waves of burning heat, ripping, scorching, tearing asunder.
- *11-12*: -| *Minor Concussion*: Somehow, you pull away mostly unscathed. `You Risk Moderate Panic and are Stunned_2 and Deaf for the next 2d6 Rounds.`
- *4-10*: Major| *Shelled*: The ripping air and wind passes through, not dead, not yet. `You begin to Bleed, are more Vulnerable by one, and Risk Moderate Panic.`
- *2-3*: Lethal| *Obliteration*: Gone. `You die.`

Physical Damage: **Catastrophic**
	*Base Damage*: 6
Might without measure, doom in the air, death passing by or through.
- *11-12*: -| *Providential Turn*: A brush, a breath of wind that hardly betrays the Doom that just passed you by. `You suffer 1 Strain.`
- *2-10*: Lethal| *Annihilation*: The obvious conclusion. `You die.`

Energy Damage: **Frost**
	*Base Damage*: 2
Black gnawing at the shafts of your bones, rime in the veins, blue lips and cracked skin. `All Frost Damage inflicts the Stunned and Off-Balance Conditions with a Duration in Turns up to the Strain suffered.`
- *12*: -| *Shiver*: A mere brush with the arctic. `You Risk Minor Panic.`
- *4-11*: Moderate| *Bite*: Numb, darkened streaks, almost like a bruise. `You Risk Moderate Panic.`
- *2-3*: Major| *Black Burn*: Deeper bites, killing at the extremities first. `Roll Major Panic Risk. You suffer a penalty of 1 to all Tests made with you hands. If you do not receive Treatment within 24 Hours, this is Permanent and cannot be removed by normal means.`

Energy Damage: **Voltaic**
	*Base Damage*: 3
Electrical power from bolts and blue arcs of light, streaks of hate that freeze the muscles and freeze the heart. `Voltaic Damage Stuns you for Rounds up to your Tier.`
- *8-12*: -| *Murmur*: A twitch as the power passes by. `You Risk Minor Panic and are Stunned for one Round for each 6 rolled.`
- *4-7*: Moderate| *Shudder*: Dendritic lesions etched across the flesh. `You Risk Moderate Panic and are Stunned_2 for one Round for each 6 rolled.`
- *2-3*: Major| *Tree-Scar*: Black lines of burned skin, clawing deep inside. `You Risk Major Panic and are Stunned_2 for each 6 rolled, and Stunned_1 until Recovery. If this Injury Incapacitates you, you die.`

Energy Damage: **Incendiary**
	*Base Damage*: 3
Burns and caustic lesions, Incendiary Risk is a near promise of lasting harm. `If you suffer sufficient Permanent Strain from Incendiary Damage to be automatically Incapacitated, you die.`
- *11-12*: -| *Superficial Burn*: A flash of pain quickly subsides as you find yourself almost unscathed. `You Risk Minor Panic.`
- *6-10*: Moderate| *1st-Degree Burn*: Bright, hot and painful, a red bloom in the senses. `You Risk Minor Panic which Inflicts Permanent Strain.`
- *4-5*: Major| *2nd-Degree Burn*: A cold, deep bite, inflammation in the skin and your own heart. `You Risk Moderate Panic which inflicts Permanent Strain.`
- *2-3*: Major| *3rd-Degree Burn*: Something worse, loss of sensation and the dread of permanent disfigurement. `You Risk Major Panic which inflicts permanent Strain and suffer a Penalty of 1 to Reflex and Body.`

Energy Damage: **Chaos**
	*Base Damage*: 3
Strange, violating energies that twist the body and mind.
- 7-12: -| *Seeing Violet*: `You suffer Strain equal to the Damage and are Frenzied for 1d6 Rounds. If this rolls 6, you cannot resist the Frenzy at all.`
- 2-6: Major| *Chaos Burn*: `You suffer a penalty of 1 to all Abilities and instantly Panic.`

Energy Damage: **Order**
	*Base Damage*: 3
The energy of perfection, with all the restrictions and inhibition demanded by flawless Order.
- *11-12*: -| *Release*: `You Risk Minor Panic.`
- *7-10*: Moderate| *Chained*: `You Risk Moderate Panic and are Castigated for one Round for each 6.`
- *2-6*: Moderate| *Shackled*: `You Risk Major Panic and are Castigated for one Round for each 6.`
#### Treating Injuries
Each Severity of Injury has associated Activities required for treatment, that is, to remove the Injury. Some of these can be performed yourself, while others require help, either for lack of Knowledge, or because you lack the ability.

**Minor Injuries**
These can be removed by Bandaging them, but Recover on their own with Rest.

**Moderate Injuries**
These have a default Recovery Time, equal to ten times the Injury Strain. At the conclusion, their effects are removed.

**Major Injuries**
You need Surgical Treatment before these even begin Recovery. If you have a Major Injury, untreated, for Days in excess of 10 minus the Injury Strain, you die from systemic infection. After Treatment, Major Injuries have a Recovery Time thrice as long as an analogous Moderate Injury.

- 2-6: Major| *Chaos Burn*: `You suffer a penalty of 1 to all Abilities and instantly Panic.`

Energy Damage: **Order**
	*Base Damage*: 3
The energy of perfection, with all the restrictions and inhibition demanded by flawless Order.
- *11-12*: -| *Release*: `You Risk Minor Panic.`
- *7-10*: Moderate| *Chained*: `You Risk Moderate Panic and are Castigated for one Round for each 6.`
- *2-6*: Moderate| *Shackled*: `You Risk Major Panic and are Castigated for one Round for each 6.`
#### Treating Injuries
Each Severity of Injury has associated Activities required for treatment, that is, to remove the Injury. Some of these can be performed yourself, while others require help, either for lack of Knowledge, or because you lack the ability.

**Minor Injuries**
These can be removed by Bandaging them, but Recover on their own with Rest.

**Moderate Injuries**
These have a default Recovery Time, equal to ten times the Injury Strain. At the conclusion, their effects are removed.

**Major Injuries**
You need Surgical Treatment before these even begin Recovery. If you have a Major Injury, untreated, for Days in excess of 10 minus the Injury Strain, you die from systemic infection. After Treatment, Major Injuries have a Recovery Time thrice as long as an analogous Moderate Injury.

body_md:
#### Panic Risk
This represents your Character briefly faltering in a moment of shock, pain, or anxiety, when circumstances briefly overwhelms them.
- Panic Risk is a rolled Pool of Chaos Dice, with a size according to its Severity.
- If any Chaos Dice in the Pool roll 6, you Panic. The sizes of these Pools are:
	*Minor*: 2| *Moderate*: 3| *Major*: 6
*Mental Resistance*
	When rolling Panic Risk, you roll fewer Chaos Dice by your Mind Bonus, minimum one.
*The Effects of Panic*
	When you Panic, you suffer Strain for each 6 rolled, and your Panic Response takes effect.
#### Corruption
The negative aspect of the psyche, Corruption represents long-term damage and dysfunction, compounding anxiety and eventual collapse.

**The Measure of Corruption**
Starting from zero, Corruption can build over time. Corruption has a Scale, depending on the value, as follows:
- 0-5: *Clear*
- 6-11: *Dark*
- 12-17: *Morbid*
- 18: *Terminal*
*The Effects of Corruption*
	The major effect of Corruption is that, when you Panic, you suffer effects corresponding to its Scale. Likewise, the more Corruption you have, the easier it is to gain more.

**Rolling Corruption**
When you suffer Major Panic, and at GM discretion when your Character is exposed to or, especially, when they enact something genuinely depraved or psychically dangerous, you roll Corruption. This is a Pool of Chaos Dice, with a number corresponding to your current Scale:
- *Clear*: 3
- *Dark*: 5
- *Morbid*: 7
*Gaining Corruption and Falling*
	For each 6 rolled, you suffer a point of Corruption. If this ever raises your Scale to Terminal, you Fall. This is a form of psychotic break, losing control of your Character to the GM. Recovery from Falling is possible, but is something the Fallen Character will always resist, usually to an extreme if not deadly degree.
#### Fixation and Depravity
Fall and recovery have other alternatives, when you would Fall, you may suffer a Fixation instead. Fixations are distorted states of mind that both strengthen and parasitize their victims. The Fixated have a unique relationship with the Corruption, namely that they actively feed on it, as their warped state feeds on them.

**Fallen**
When you suffer a Fixation, you shed all Corruption, but lose your Archetype and associated effects. Instead, you gain the effects of the Fixation, which has its own Feat and Panic Response.

**Depravity**
Instead of a Scale, your Corruption gains a numerical Bonus, like an Ability, with a Value equal to (1 plus every six Corruption.) So, just after Falling, your Bonus would be 1, 2 if you gained 6 Corruption, 3 for 12, etc. This Bonus is called your Depravity, and scales the effects of your Fixation.

**Permanence**
Suffering a Fixation has no natural path to Recovery and is essentially a defining choice, unless your Character receives some extraordinary blessing like genuine divine intervention.

**Finality**
If you ever suffer 18 or more Corruption after suffering a Fixation, your psyche is totally broken, reducing you to a violent, dangerous husk; an NPC under the control of the GM with no hope of regaining even a facsimile of sanity.
#### The Fixations
Fixation: **The Inverse Panopticon**
	*"They hate me"*
	*Feat*: False Armor
	`When you roll Panic Risk, you can reduce the Pool by your Depravity.`
	*Panic Response*: Fracture
	*"Run, run, run run r-"*
	`You are compelled to flee, as fast as you are able.`

Fixation: **Void**
	*"Only I exist"*
	*Feat*: Head Like a Hole
	`You may add your Depravity to any Test to manipulate another.`
	*Panic Response*: Perfection
	*"Give them nothing"*
	`You gain a Boon to all Tests for the next Minute, but every time you fail, you Risk Minor Panic. Critically Failing raises this Severity to Major.`

Fixation: **A Hungry Wound**
	*"They should fear me"*
	*Feat*: Power from the Dark
	`You may add your Depravity to Attacks and can roll Corruption to make the Damage more Vicious by your Tier.`
	*Panic Response*: Burn
	*"Destroy Everything"*
	`You are Frenzied and compelled to kill the closest living thing for Minutes up to your Corruption.`

Fixation: **The Obverse Bend**
	*"Don't tell me what to do"*
	*Feat*: Only Survivor
	`You gain a Bonus to all Abilities up to your Depravity, but each Ally within as many Meters reduces this by one.`
	*Panic Response*: Anti-Synergy
	*"I don't need you"*
	`For the next Minute, your Allies suffer the same penalty as you to their Abilities from your Depravity.`

Fixation: **The Narrow Way**
	*"I need it"*
	*Feat*: Purity
	`You can ignore all other sources of Panic Risk, and gain a repository of Boons up to twice your Depravity to be used for any reason. These replenish when your Rest. However, you have a singular, highly specific Goal. If you fail to pursue or follow it, you suffer Major Panic Risk. Wore, if you ever achieve your Goal, you instantly fall.`
	*Panic Response*: Collapse
	*"No, no, no no no no nononononononononononnono"*
	`You suffer 1d6 Corruption.`

name: Rest and Catching your Breath
summary: General Activity: Catching your Breath After 10 Minutes or so of inactivity, you shed all Standard Strain. An Hour of light Activity also counts for Catching your Breath. Collaboration: All participants gain the benefit.
body_md:
General Activity: **Catching your Breath**
	`After 10 Minutes or so of inactivity, you shed all Standard Strain. An Hour of light Activity also counts for Catching your Breath.`
	*Collaboration*: All participants gain the benefit.

General Activity: **Rest**
	`You Spend Watches to gain the following benefits, depending on the amount of time:`
	- One Watch: `You shed all Standard Strain and Persistent up to your Tier.`
	- Two Watches: `You shed all Standard Strain and half your Persistent.`
	- Three Watches: `You shed all Standard and Persistent Strain.`
	- Four Watches: `As three, and all your Injuries also reduce their Recovery time by one.`
	*Degradation*
	`Each Day you spend without Resting at all inflicts 1 Permanent Strain, which can only be removed by Resting for three Watches.`
	*Collaboration*: Resting together, beyond comradery, has little effect.

name: Disease and Addictions
summary: Diseases represent corruption of the body by microbial, fungal, or viral life and other invasive forces. Each Disease is unique as are the ways of contracting and curing them.
body_md:
#### Disease
Diseases represent corruption of the body by microbial, fungal, or viral life and other invasive forces. Each Disease is unique as are the ways of contracting and curing them.

In general, a Disease has the following elements:
- **Risk**: which gives an initial roll or procedure for contracting it. Contracting a Disease makes you Infected.
- **Progression**: when Infected, this quantifies how the Disease worsens.
- **Stages**: a Tiered system (beginning at 0, Infection), that gives symptoms and effects as the Disease progresses.
- **Resolution**: The manner by which the Disease can be Recovered from, if at all.
#### Addictions
An Addiction is a dependency on a single substance which is always an Item with the Addictive Quality, such that you cannot adequately function without it. When you fail to consume the Item within its Secondary Duration, you enter Withdrawal and suffer effects depending on the substance. Addictions can be recovered from by suffering withdrawal for an amount of time equal to twice its Tertiary Duration. Each use of the substance while in withdrawal resets the remaining time, not exceeding the total. Finally, you can choose to ingest lower-than-active doses of a substance (which counts as half of a use of the Item,) to avoid the negative effects of withdrawal while contributing half that time to recovery.
